records.central_bank: National Bank of Moldova (Banca Naţională a Moldovei)
records.category: procurement and budget-compliance irregularities found by the supreme audit institution
records.people: Tatiana Ivanicichina (deputy governor, member of the Supervisory Board); Aliona Vacariţa (director, Budget, Finance and Accounting Department); Natalia Zabolotnii (director, Strategy, Organisation and Human Resources Department); Olga Pisarenco (head of the Procurement and Contract Management Division)
records.summary: Moldova's Court of Accounts, by Decision no.6 of 9 February 2024, approved a compliance audit of the National Bank of Moldova's expenditure estimates and investment allocations for 2019-2022 and recorded findings against the Bank: essential planning principles (prudence, consultation, exhaustiveness, responsibility, optimisation, rationality and efficiency) were not observed, leaving about 192.0 million lei of approved expenditure unused (16.9%) and about 147.4 million lei of approved investment allocations unused (65.3%); 1.2 million lei of material aid was paid to retired former employees in the absence of distinct and clear rules; in 2021 the Bank's own working group decided to refer documents for verification over suspicions of distortion of competition in a works procurement, but the referral was never sent to the Competition Council; and 3.2 million lei of repair works were charged to the expenditure estimate instead of being added to the value of the asset although the IAS 16 recognition criteria were met. A protocol office at the Holercani guesthouse carried on the Bank's balance sheet since a 1998 Government order is still not registered as public property, a fact the Court had already found in 2015.
records.source_title: Curtea de Conturi a Republicii Moldova, Hotărârea nr.6 din 09 februarie 2024 cu privire la Raportul de audit al conformităţii devizelor de cheltuieli şi alocaţiilor pentru investiţii ale Băncii Naţionale a Moldovei pe anii 2019-2022
records.quote: demersul nu a fost expediat Consiliului Concurenţei
records.detail: Every figure, name and date above is printed in the decision itself: the four named Bank officials are listed in the opening paragraph as attending the Court's video-format sitting, and the 2015 precedent is footnote 8, Court of Accounts Decision no.22 of 06.07.2015 on the compliance audit of the execution of the expenditure estimate at the National Bank. The audit was carried out under art.32(7) of Law no.260 of 07.12.2017 and art.21(2) of Law no.548 of 21.07.1995, which confine the Court's external audit of the Bank to the legality and regularity of its expenditure estimates and investment allocations and exclude monetary and exchange-rate policy and reserve management. This is a separate episode from the record the map already holds for Moldova, which is the 2012-2016 criminal investigation of Dorin Drăguţanu and other officials over the banking frauds: different years, different people, different conduct, different document.

blanks.kind: confirmed blank (for this document and year)
blanks.note: Inversion test run on the State Audit Office's own annual report. Државен завод за ревизија, Годишен извештај за 2025 (dzr.mk/sites/default/files/2026-06/GI_2025_FINAL_mkd_0.pdf, 11.4 MB, 22,327 lines of extracted text) downloaded and grepped in full after Unicode NFKC normalisation for 'Народна банка', 'НБРСМ' and 'НБРМ'. There is exactly one hit in the whole report and it is a table column header, 'Повлечени средства (на сметка во НБРСМ)' — drawn funds held in an account at the National Bank — in the state-debt tables. The National Bank does not appear anywhere in the report as an audited entity, so the DZR performed no audit of it in that reporting year. This does NOT close the series: arhiva.dzr.mk does hold a per-entity DZR report on the National Bank (Narodna%20banka%20na%20Republika%20Makedonija.doc), and the map already files that one as a 2005-03-04 state-audit event, so other years of the archive remain a live lead. Host note: dzr.mk serves plain curl fine, unlike nbrm.mk.

The named lead is found and it is a real per-entity series. The Office of the Auditor General has a dedicated Central Bank of Solomon Islands page under Financial Audits > Government Agencies > Statutory Authorities (oag.gov.sb/audit-reports-footer/financial-audits/government-agencies-financial/statutory-authorities/central-bank-of-solomon-islands-cbsi.html), listing twelve documents: CBSI financial-statement opinions for 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019, plus a separate fuller 'CBSI audit report for 2019'. That fullest one was downloaded (item 255, 4.1 MB, 48 pages, a scan with no text layer, OCRed at 170 dpi with tesseract). It is the Bank's Annual Statement of Accounts for the year ended 31 December 2019 with the Auditor-General's report at pages 5-7. The opinion is UNMODIFIED: the financial statements give a true and fair view in accordance with IFRS. There is no qualification, no emphasis of matter and no reported irregularity; the only reservation anywhere in it is a note in the Other Information section that not all other information was available at the date of signing, which is a reporting-timing limitation and not a finding. So the 2019 audit is a clean opinion and therefore a blank. The nine earlier documents are each titled 'financial statement opinion' and were not opened, so 2010-2018 is 'not reached' rather than clean. Host note: oag.gov.sb serves both its HTML index and its /file.html document endpoints to plain curl without trouble, which is new — round 71 recorded pacliirms.austlii.edu.au as returning nothing, and that separate court-judgment vein was not retried here.

The Auditor-General vein is tested and it does not reach the Bank of Namibia. Round 71's host note was used: bon.com.na/getattachment/<guid>/.aspx served, at guid 3f7c3a08-7399-4cd8-b00f-a70bf7034f53, the 'Summary report of the Auditor-General on the accounts of the Government of Namibia for the financial year ended 31 March 2012', report no 96/2013 (1.38 MB, 74,338 characters of text), downloaded and grepped in full. 'Bank of Namibia' occurs five times and never as an audited entity: once in the explanation of unprocessed cheques held at the Bank, twice in the paragraph 2.9 Shares schedule of state shareholdings (as 'Bank of Namibia' and 'Bank of Namibia (FIC)'), and once in the dividends-received schedule. The Agricultural Bank and the Development Bank of Namibia appear in the same lists. Grepping the whole report for fraud, disciplinary, misconduct, irregular, embezzl, theft, dismiss, whistle and ethics returned only two hits, both in the standard auditor's-responsibilities boilerplate at lines 123-124. So the Auditor-General treats the Bank of Namibia as a state investment and a counterparty, not as an audited body, which is what the Bank of Namibia Act's own external-auditor arrangement would predict. The Bank's own annual report remains an untried route for an internal-discipline disclosure.

Round 72's first named lead, the Director of Audit's annual report, could not be reached: a search for Director of Audit Mauritius findings on the Bank of Mauritius returned only Bank of Mauritius and commercial-bank annual reports, a COMESA external audit report and two Scribd uploads, and no Director of Audit document naming the Bank. So the second named vein was tried instead, the Bank's own annual report. Bank of Mauritius Annual Report 2025 (bom.mu/sites/default/files/bom_ar_2025_web.pdf, 473,881 characters) — curl confirms round 72's host note, bom.mu returns HTTP 000 with a zero-byte transfer through the proxy, and WebFetch serves it. The first 100,000 characters, which carry the governance material, report NO disciplinary finding, fraud, irregularity, investigation or forensic audit concerning the Bank or its staff. Two items sit near the subject and neither is a record: the Audit and Risk Committee is described as overseeing internal controls and legal compliance and as having held two meetings during FY2024-25, with no findings reported; and the report records that on 29 August 2025 Mr Gerard Sanspeur tendered his resignation with immediate effect as Second Deputy Governor, giving no reason, which under the rules is an unexplained exit and not a record on either row. Characters 100,000 onward were not read for want of budget, so the integrity and internal-audit sections deeper in the report are 'not reached'. Round 71's finding still holds that every press lead a search surfaces is the Seegolam and Padayachy Mauritius Investment Corporation episode the map already holds.

Second French-language search of the Cour des comptes de Madagascar's published output, this time aimed squarely at the rapport public annuel and at any control of the Banque Centrale de Madagascar or BFM. It returned, again, everything but the central bank: the contaminated-seed state scandal (allafrica, March 2026), the scathing report on large infrastructure projects (allafrica, March 2026), the sweep of 33 ministries (allafrica, February 2026), the 2022 performance report and the 2024-25 reports mirrored at aisccuf.org, the November 2025 launch of a large audit at the Ministry of Economy and Finance, an INTOSAI Journal piece on the Court's jurisdictional control, three IMF country reports and a World Bank ROSC. Nothing in two rounds of searching names the BFM as an audited body. The Court's own report index on its own host still has not been opened, so the honest label is that the search route is exhausted while the index route is untested. The map's one MDG record remains the 2026 pressure allegation.

A Portuguese search for Camara de Contas audit reports naming the Banco Central de Timor-Leste returned no such report. The nearest thing to an inversion test was opened: the VII Constitutional Government's press release of 21 February 2018, 'Pedidos de Auditoria a Camara de Contas do TSAFC' (timor-leste.gov.tl/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/CI-Auditorias.pdf, 350 KB), in which Prime Minister Mari Alkatiri formalises audit requests to the Camara de Contas covering the Treasury, the Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications, the ADN, the Infrastructure Fund and the Ministry of Tourism for 9 August 2012 to 14 September 2017, following an earlier request of 6 February covering the ARAEOA. The document was grepped for 'Banco Central' and 'BCTL' with zero hits, so the central bank is absent from the list. This is a weak inversion test: it is the government's own list of requested audits, not the Camara's list of audited bodies, so it shows only that the 2018 round of requests did not reach the BCTL. The Camara's own report index is still unopened. Note for the next round that the country's single existing case record is counterparty_only, a Ministry of Finance finding, so a national finding whose subject is the BCTL itself would still be Timor-Leste's first colouring record.

Third Uzbek-language search for Accounts Chamber (Hisob palatasi) inspection results naming the Central Bank, this time phrased for detected violations. It returned no Hisob palatasi document at all. Every result is the Central Bank as DETECTOR, which the row excludes by rule: yuz.uz and anhor.uz on the Central Bank fining seven banks, spot.uz on bank fines in June 2026 and November 2025, kun.uz on three commercial banks fined in October 2025 for consumer-rights breaches, anhor.uz on eight banks fined over dealings with consumers, plus two lex.uz statutes and the Bank's own anti-corruption overview PDF on cbu.uz. So on three rounds of searching no Accounts Chamber document naming the Central Bank of Uzbekistan has surfaced; the Chamber's own report index remains the only untried route. The map's existing UZB record, the 2025 internal-discipline finding out of the Bank's own report, was already the product of the bank's-own-report vein, so that vein is used up here too.

Arabic search of the State Audit Bureau (ديوان المحاسبة) for observations and violations naming the Central Bank of Kuwait. It returned nine results and not one concerns the Central Bank: Al-Anba newspaper page scans from 21 September 2020 and 17 November 2009, Al-Arabiya on a civil-aviation contract, Al-Jarida on the municipality's court defence costs, on the Public Authority for Housing Welfare failing the Bureau's test and on imprecision in the Ministry of Higher Education's budget estimates, an Al-Rai article, an ARABOSAI success-story PDF and a Google Docs export. The Bureau's reports to the National Assembly are published as parliamentary documents rather than as a per-entity series on its own site, and no index of audited entities surfaced, so no inversion test was possible. Nothing was fetched for Kuwait. Label this vein closed on search and the Bureau's own publications index still not reached.

The named document could not be opened. A search for Office of the Auditor General findings on the National Bank of Rwanda returned the OAG's own host twice — oag.gov.rw/fileadmin/REPORTS/AUDITOR_GENERAL_PRESENTS_2023_ANNUAL_AUDIT_REPORT_TO_PARLIAMENT.pdf and a news page for the 2024 presentation — plus KT Press and New Times summaries of the 2022-23 and 2024 reports, an AllAfrica piece headlined 'Clean Audits Are Progress, Not Cause for Complacency', the Parliament's own reports and annual-reports index pages, an IMF publication and a World Bank project audit text. The OAG PDF was fetched and returned HTTP 404 with a 196-byte body, so nothing was read. The press summaries list the AG's recurring themes and none of them names the National Bank. The route to try next is the Parliament's own reports index at parliament.gov.rw/resources/reports, which carries the Public Accounts Committee's reports on the AG's findings, and the OAG's own report index rather than the fileadmin path. Round 72's separate court vein is already recorded as closed.

No document opened and no search spent. Carried forward unchanged from rounds 71 and 72. have_cases and have_events were read before any research (the 2026 convictions of Khamphout and Aod over cheap FX to insiders, and the 1995 banking law event), so the duplicate check is done. The State Audit Organisation of Laos has no index that any earlier round has surfaced, and bol.gov.la is already recorded as script-rendered and invisible to both tools.

No Lesotho document opened; budget went to the countries whose named document proved to exist. have_cases and have_events read: the February 2024 charge over the R57 theft from the Central Bank of Lesotho, and the June 2026 Public Accounts Committee call for a forensic audit into the missing M3.9 billion, which is already filed as a parliamentary-inquiry event and must not be refiled as a case. The standing leads are unchanged: the Office of the Auditor General Lesotho's own report index, and the National Assembly's published PAC minutes.

Not retried. Round 71's host finding is the reason: no al.gov.mo attachment is reachable by either tool, three of them returning an identical 117-byte body to curl and an HTML meta-refresh to WebFetch, so the Comissariado da Auditoria's per-subject reports cannot be opened from here, and the gov.mo annual policy-lines documents carry no list of audited entities, so no inversion test exists. Spending this round's remaining budget on the same host would have repeated a known failure.

No Mauritanian document opened. have_cases and have_events read: the 2020 arrest of a Banque Centrale de Mauritanie employee and others over a missing million dollars, and the July 2004 dismissal of the central bank chief. The standing leads are unchanged and untested: the Cour des comptes de Mauritanie annual report, and the Banque Centrale de Mauritanie's own published accounts.

No Sao Tomean document opened. have_cases and have_events read: the 2006 procurement allegation against governor Maria do Carmo Silveira, which is filed as both a case and the June 2006 dismissal event, so it is one episode under two descriptions and a second must be away from it. The standing leads are unchanged: the Tribunal de Contas de Sao Tome e Principe's reports, and the Assembleia Nacional diaries mirrored by the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies at www2.camara.leg.br/saotomeeprincipe.

No document opened. have_cases and have_events read: the OeBS banknote-printing kickback verdicts naming unnamed Central Bank of Syria decision makers for 2005-2011, the 2002 statutory event, and the February 2012 EU asset freeze. The Central Agency for Financial Inspection publishes nothing that any round has surfaced, and no search was spent here. Note for whoever does: an Arabic PDF from cb.gov.sy will need NFKC normalisation before grepping, as brief_common.md sets out.

Deprioritised and not worked, for the second round running, and the reason should be fixed in the generator rather than re-reported. have_cases shows Thailand already holds TWO corruption-case records — Rerngchai Marakanond, acquitted, and Surapong Suebwonglee with the conflicted selection-committee appointments, convicted — plus five entries on the removals and pressure row. It is therefore not a member of the exactly-one set the assignment says it came from, and a third record there buys less than a second anywhere else in the slice. The State Audit Office of Thailand annual-report lead is untouched and still valid if anyone wants a third.

No Tajik audit-chamber document fetched, for the third round running. have_cases and have_events read: the IMF's creative-accounting finding against National Bank of Tajikistan management for 2004-2008, and the 2011 NBT law event. The Agency for State Financial Control and the Fight against Corruption publishes no report index that any round has surfaced, and nothing was spent here this round, so Tajikistan is still genuinely untested on the audit-institution vein rather than clean.

Not retried, and it should not be retried on this vein. Turkmenistan is already recorded in closed_negatives as publishing no annual report and no audited financial statements at all: cbt.tm answers 403 to curl, renders through WebFetch, and its only publications entry is a bank-news journal, 'Bank habarlary'. The documentary base that the supreme-audit-institution vein and the bank's-own-report vein both require does not exist for this country, so the blank is structural rather than a search failure. The map's one case record is the 1992-2002 charge against former chairman Khudaiberdi Orazov.

Deprioritised and not worked. have_cases shows Tonga already holds TWO records — the conviction of a Senior Exchange Control Officer, and the board conflict-of-interest case dismissed at TOCA 2025/25 — and the assignment's own note for the Pacific countries says so in passing. It is not on exactly-one for this row. The Tonga Auditor General's reports remain a valid lead for a third.

No search or fetch spent on Venezuela for the third round running, so round 71's note still stands untested: the Contraloria General de la Republica de Venezuela's per-entity reports are the nominal route and are unlikely to be published for the BCV, but that has not been checked and should not be assumed. have_cases and have_events read: the January 2020 charges over sham services in the BCV's Payments and Taxes and Procurement and Supply departments, the January 2017 dismissal, and the July 2022 London High Court ruling on the gold. The country has still not been tested.

Not re-run, as the assignment instructs. Samoa is already a documented negative on this vein in closed_negatives: the Samoa Audit Office matters that search returns have as their subjects the Ministry of Health's procurement, the Ministry of Finance's accounts division and the Samoa Land Corporation. Samoa also already holds two case records, one of them the 2024 internal-discipline finding out of the Central Bank's own 2023-2024 annual report, so the bank's-own-report vein is used up here as well.

checked_not_in_assignment: Serbia, Turkey, Mexico, Czechia and Nicaragua were read only as the worked examples named in the briefs, and nothing was filed for any of them.

BTN, HKG, MYS, PAK and PNG appear in the quoted round-71 and round-72 notes carried into my assignment. I did not research any of them and filed nothing, per the assignment's explicit warning that all five were worked in those rounds and three were filed.

Moldova's own decision names an earlier audit of the same bank, Court of Accounts Decision no.22 of 06.07.2015 on the compliance audit of the execution of the expenditure estimate at the National Bank of Moldova (footnote 8 of hcc_nr.6_din_09.02.2024.pdf). That is a different document, different years and probably its own findings, so it is a live candidate for a THIRD Moldovan record. I did not open it and did not file it, because Moldova moves off exactly-one on the 2024 decision alone and another country's second was worth more.

Fiji's PricewaterhouseCoopers office appears in the Solomon Islands auditor's report as the firm the Auditor-General contracted to assist the CBSI audit. I checked party_names.json: PricewaterhouseCoopers is already carried on the map in several spellings. I filed no tie, because the external-auditors row is not my row and nobody asked me for it; recording it here so the auditors row can pick it up. The wording on the page is that the Auditor-General 'contracted PricewaterhouseCoopers Fiji, which is part of the PricewaterhouseCoopers International network, to assist me to audit' the Bank's financial statements, and that text is OCR of a scan, so it should be re-read from the source before being quoted.
leads_not_opened: SLB: nine further CBSI financial-statement audit opinions on oag.gov.sb for 2010 through 2018, each a separate document at /audit-reports-footer/financial-audits/government-agencies-financial/statutory-authorities/central-bank-of-solomon-islands-cbsi/<id>-<slug>/file.html, ids 61 through 66 and 247 through 249. The host serves these to plain curl. They are scans needing OCR, about a minute each. Any one carrying a qualification or an emphasis of matter is a record.

MKD: arhiva.dzr.mk holds per-entity State Audit Office reports and serves them to curl; the National Bank one already on the map is dated 2005-03-04 and is filed as an event, so other years of the same series are the cheapest remaining MKD candidate.

MUS: Bank of Mauritius Annual Report 2025, characters 100,000 to 473,881, via WebFetch with offset (bom.mu refuses curl). The governance chapter read clean; the internal-audit and compliance sections deeper in the report were not reached.

RWA: parliament.gov.rw/resources/reports for the Public Accounts Committee's reports on the Auditor-General's findings, and the OAG's own report index rather than the /fileadmin/REPORTS/ path, which 404s.

TWN: www.cy.gov.tw/AP_HOME/Op_Upload/eDoc/ gazette PDFs still return a 1,161-byte HTML error body to curl even with the path percent-encoded, so they need WebFetch. The host that DID work is cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/<id>, which served a document to plain curl; incrementing or searching that id space is the route to the full text of corrective-measure case 114財正0002 and to others naming 中央銀行, 中央印製廠 or 中央造幣廠.
TLS and MDG: both audit institutions' own report indexes, which no round has yet opened. For both countries every negative so far is a search negative, not a document negative.
